Perfect pizza & pasta, with great staff and love the industrial vibe!
Oct 2025 • Couples
My partner had eaten here a number of times and wanted me to try the pizza and pasta, and I was definitely not disappointed. The vibe is modern with an industrial look; concrete mixes with exposed brickwork but it feels cosy not cold. 

You wait for a table to be free downstairs at the entrance before ascending the stairs (which may be a little narrow for some). 

We were on the top floor and the place was buzzing with busy servers and happy customers. 

Our friendly waiter happily made a few recommendations but we had decided on pizza and also the crab pasta, washed down with a couple of cold in-house beers. 

From our perch we could watch our pizzas being prepared below! 

Our 1/2 & 1/2 pizza consisted of 3 cheese on one side and on the other, Burrata Parma Ham. It was wonderful, with a light and crisp base and cooked to perfection. 

The Crab tomato Cream Spaghetti was also delicious; fresh, light and already a firm favourite. 
Very much looking forward to our next visit to Saigon - and to PIZZA 4 P’S.

Don't Bother
Mar 2026 • Couples
Over the years I've eaten at 4P's multiple times in different cities and can tell you the pizza is monumentally failure compared to pizza in Europe, Canada and the US. 
Pizza is first and foremost all about the dough, the crust. You want a chard, crispy result. Although you may see some blackened bits on 4Ps pizza, the dough has a horrible white bread consistency. Like cheap doughy tasteless, characterless white bread. The toppings were decent though it’s not enough to save this sinking ship.
I fail to see what the hype is all about.

Apparently just hype, a social media snowball effect. People at my table were saying Pizza hut is so much better, which is itself substandard.
Don’t waste your time or money.

During my recent trip, a few of the local Vietnamese recommended my friends and I to try the food at this place, which has quite a few branches peppered around the whole city. I found it quite interesting that the locals would recommend a non-Vietnamese restaurant to a tourist.

Since we were at Ben Thanh market in the morning, we went to the outlet nearby for lunch. They do a de-constructed look for the decor, and it all looked quite pleasant and rustic. I like the large window openings that allow very uninhibited views of the outside street hustle and bustle. There is also plenty of glass louvres around, which looks pretty but seems dangerous as it is not wired glass.

I did find the entrance steps leading up to the dining area to be quite hazardous. If someone fell down the stairs and rolled down to the landing, he/she would be greeted by a wall of glass louvers that are unshielded and would cause quite an injury. Or the person would crash through the glass louvres, and land on the road outside.

The food lived up to my expectations as described by the locals who recommended the restaurant. My friend and I shared a half-and-half pizza, as well as their famous crab pasta (685,000 VND). The pizza dough was fluffy and flavourful, and definitely passed my requirements of what makes a good pizza.

But the star of this lunch was the crab pasta. It looks rather simple, but packed full of flavour. I did wish that they would add more crab meat to what is more of a garnish. Personally, I really loved the creamy flavour of the pasta sauce, but this is best avoided if one is watching one's cholesterol intake, or simply do not like crab roe (might be a bit fishy for some).

I wish I had more stomach room to order more food, as we had a very heavy breakfast at the hotel. This was a very good recommendation, and I look forward to eating at this place the next time I am visiting Ho Chi Minh City.

Secondly, someone may not like it, and being on top it’s easy to remove.

2. This is optional, but advised, the cooking time is a bit too low, I would add 15-25 seconds because more than once pasta was under cooked and tomato sauce was too liquid, making pizza not crunchy.

FOOD (1.2m dongs / 37 GBP for two with alcoholic drinks) 
So we had 2 starters each including some sort of garlic bread with parma ham with a houmous like dip. As the choice of pizza is super hard to make, they offer you the possibility of half half. So I went half European style Parma Ham with Burrata and half Asian style with Japanese Ginger Pork. As mentioned they have a few regular European looking toppings as well as some more innovative Asian ones such as Tandoori Chicken Curry, Salmon Miso Cream, Calamari Seaweed, Teriyaki Chicken, Soy Garlic Beef, etc. You will have trouble deciding as they all look delicious. 
With this, we had a couple of Long Island Ice Teas and a few beers. 

The place is not cheap in my opinion, even though you can get a pizza for about 5£. For a real experience which includes really tasty burrata, your looking at 10-15£ per person. We kind of overdid it on the drinks... 

STAFF/SERVICE
Very professional service, friendly, English-speaking, organised, etc. 
Food was served decently fast considering the high amount of customers. 

ATMOSPHERE/LOCATION
This is a chain across Vietnam as far as I am concerned, I saw some in Hanoi as well as HCM so just look for your closest one. 
The atmosphere is very Western in my opinion: it is nicely decorated, the tables are clean, new, tidy and spacious and so are the nice seats with bench they offer. The place itself is pretty huge, easily accommodating 60-100 customers I'd say. 

CONCLUSION: I STRONGLY RECOMMEND AND WOULD RETURN

The dough had a nice taste, was a bit soggy in the middle but nice and crunchy on the outside crust. 
It is kind of large restaurant with a posh modern industrial interior. They also have tables on a nice terrace for those who want to sit outside and/or smoke.
Staff is friendly. The waitress that took my order might improve her English skills a bit to be able to answer customers questions regarding their different dishes. At 462.000 VND (just over 20 USD) including VAT this is also one of the most expensive pizzas I ever had so now I know why they don’t mention prices on their website. However I have to admit that they also serve somewhat cheaper pizzas starting at around 150.000 VND for an ordinary Margherita.

Conclusion: If you crave a really good pizza, get a table immediately. If your are on a tighter budget you might not want to order the Burrata pizzas.

Popular place but overrated
Oct 2017
I visit Pizza 4P's on a number of occasions just because they are around from where I work and the pasta is quite ok. 

There is a lot of hype around this chain. And indeed it is an ok place but not more. I review in general as I visit the places often. 

1. Reservation
You need to book beforehand. Lunch time it is impossible to get a table without booking and during dinner times it will be difficult to get a table; if you get one you will be restricted in time. 
Note that even if you book a table up front they sometimes conveniently miss that booking - probably because they overbooked the place; not too often though. 

2. Service
Service is ok; better at the place behind BT market than it is in D7 or at 8/15 LTT. In the latter one the service is actually quite bad; you have to think for them in order to get what you want. 

3. Pizza
Pizza is good size and of good taste. Crust is good and the ingredients are fresh-ish. Don't do the mistake and order this massive buffalo cheese on your pizza; it just soaks the whole thing up and the crust is all wet and soaky. 
The cheese pizza is ok too; don't order the blue cheese though, very strong which is not my favorite on a pizza. 
The sushi tuff on a pizza - I have never ordered as I don't think that belongs on a pizza; but a friend of mine likes it and finds it ok. Your choice. 

4. Pasta
The place should be called Pasta 4P's as the pasta is really nice. Fresh and well cooked to perfection - in all outlets. Recommend the salmon pasta. 

5. Pricing
Considering that you get average pizza for quite a high price, I find the pricing too much. For pasta it's ok. Drinks are well priced. 

6. Conclusion
A place to go if you want to be seen by the hip ones. Wouldn't go there for the food as the ambience is also just ok. I return for pastas only.

We went here as we were in Vietnam for 2 weeks and didn't want to eat traditional food everyday. The place itself is in district 1 so central but off a main road up a small road and at the end of another narrow road so we had to ask as it's hidden for first timers. 

This is a Japanese pizzeria in Vietnam, what's great about it is all produce is locally sourced and produced in farms in Vietnam. The burrata and cheeses used are produced by the restaurant working with farmers in Da Lat. You can also see the team in action on the restaurant floor making the pizzas.

When you get to the door the restaurant is always busy with families, couples, friends and business people. 

The menu is based on all fresh ingredients with different cheese options. You can also get half and half pizza, burrata cheese (whole mozzarella in middle) or classics with lots of Italian choices as well as Japanese twists (chicken teriyaki).

We went there twice on our trip as we loved this pizza so much! 

We ordered garlic strips with hummus, egg plant, chicken teriyaki half and half and one burrata Parma ham (the waiter slices the burrata cheese upon serving mozzarella) the first time - delicious, so fresh and organic tasty with the Parma ham. Favourite was the egg plant it only had fresh mozzarella but you can ask for 4 or 5 other cheeses to be added onto your pizza.

The second time we ordered the egg plant, burrata Parma ham and and a fresh pasta dish which was a special prawn. All again was so delicious and the dough just melts in your mouth. The pasta is freshly made and so yummy full of flavour and it's exactly like being in Italy! 

Would highly recommend this place for exceptional food, service and experience. Reasonably priced too :) all round feel good place without making you feel guilty for eating pizza as it's quite healthy depending on what you order.

One will say it's a matter of taste and it probably is, but the layout of the place, a small table between 2 other tables among many others lined up along a wall, didn't make us want to stay and hang out for too long... There're cozier places. 
Service was really good, the waiting staff was very attentive and dishes came out quickly, which is a good thing. 
Now food. As I said I was expecting more.. You can tell all the ingredients are really fresh, but taste-wise there was nothing impressive at all. We had 2 appetizers and 2 half-half pizzas (after almost getting lost in the menu since it's more like an encyclopedia of food really) so tried a few things and overall it was all bland. Lacked of basic salt and pepper, in addition to just taste... The chorizo/salami pizza was good, but the mushrooms and Parma ham/burrata were nothing crazy. 3 cheeses: don't waste anytime trying it, it's a mix of bland melted cheeses, very disappointed since I am a true cheese lover. 
Wine selection was big, and the rose we had was good. 
Prices are ok. 
Overall, I would not recommend Pizza 4P's to anyone, just because you can find food with way more taste around the city. The 2 stars are for the service and the freshness of the ingredients, but that doesn't make a good restaurant.
